results.title: Federated Differential Privacy Constraints
results.content: * Federated differential privacy constraints are formal mechanisms in distributed learning that protect individual data by perturbing updates, clipping gradients, and ensuring secure aggregation. Federated differential privacy constraints refer to the formal, system-wide mechanisms by which privacy is enforced in federated learning (FL), ensuring that the sensitive information of data contributors—such as individual-level records at each client, medical silos, or edge devices—remains protected, even when model updates are collaboratively computed and shared. In federated settings, the privacy constraint is typically formalized as a per-client or per-data record differential privacy guarantee applied to the outputs of local computation and communication:. * **Strong and Weak Federated f-Differential Privacy:** Some frameworks define trade-off functions on hypothesis tests over outputs, strengthening classic DP to record-level or client-level adversary models (Zheng et al., 2021). * **Zero-Concentrated Differential Privacy (zCDP) / Renyi DP:** zCDP composes over many local updates with tighter bounds, yielding privacy loss of the form ρ=Δ22​/(2σ2), facilitating reduced noise addition for the same end-to-end constraint (Hu et al., 2020). 5. **Personalized and Adaptive Mechanisms:** Personalized graph FL and federated f-DP frameworks adapt privacy parameters across heterogeneous client clusters or allow per-client or per-record trade-offs (Gauthier et al., 2023, Zheng et al., 2021). * **Phase Transitions:** In federated nonparametric hypothesis testing under DP constraints, statistical detectability thresholds (minimax separation) exhibit phase transitions depending jointly on sample size, noise level, privacy budget, and the presence/absence of shared randomness (Cai et al., 10 Jun 2024). * **Finance and Synthetic Data Generation:** Practical frameworks (DP-Fed-FinDiff) integrate DP mechanisms with federated diffusion models for regulated domains, illustrating the strong trade-off between utility (data fidelity) and privacy, especially as privacy budgets vary (Sattarov et al., 20 Dec 2024). Federated differential privacy constraints provide formal privacy guarantees for distributed learning by requiring every participant (client, device, or site) to perturb outputs or updates such that the impact of any single data record (or client, under strong notions) is mathematically bounded. results.content: # Federated Learning with Local Differential Privacy: Trade-Offs Between Privacy, Utility, and Communication. ### Heterogeneous Differential-Private Federated Learning: Trading Privacy for Utility Truthfully. This work proposes a heterogeneous differential-private federated learning framework, named HDP-FL, which captures the variation of privacy attitudes with truthful incentives and designs a contract-based incentive mechanism, which encourages clients to truthfully reveal private attitudes and contribute to learning as desired. ### Clients Collaborate: Flexible Differentially Private Federated Learning with Guaranteed Improvement of Utility-Privacy Trade-off. ### LDP-FL: Practical Private Aggregation in Federated Learning with Local Differential Privacy. A novel design of local differential privacy mechanism for federated learning that makes the local weights update differentially private by adapting to the varying ranges at different layers of a deep neural network, which introduces a smaller variance of the estimated model weights, especially for deeper models. This paper presents LDP-Fed, a novel federated learning system with a formal privacy guarantee using local differential privacy (LDP) for the repeated collection of model training parameters in the federated training of large-scale neural networks over multiple individual participants' private datasets.

results.title: Secure Federated Learning with Differential Privacy and Homomorphic Encryption | by Sumedh Kate | Medium
results.content: While HE makes it possible to perform secure calculations on encrypted model updates, DP adds mathematical guarantees against data leakage. · Local DP: Before sending their updates to the server, clients add noise to them; this increases privacy but also makes them noisier. Incorporating Differential Privacy (DP) into Federated Learning to safeguard user data may impact the performance of the final model. Significant technical challenges arise when Differential Privacy (DP) and Homomorphic Encryption (HE) are combined in Federated Learning (FL). These updates are protected in two ways: homomorphic encryption (using schemes like Paillier) makes sure updates stay encrypted during aggregation, preventing even the coordinating server from accessing sensitive information, and differential privacy adds precisely calibrated mathematical noise (usually with ε=2) to prevent reconstruction of individual records. Strong dual protection is provided for these updates: CKKS homomorphic encryption enables safe aggregation of updates across banks without ever decrypting sensitive data, and differential privacy with ε=1 adds mathematical noise to prevent inference about specific transactions.
